ownership_reason: Only the gold's walk holds the path walked so far, and a '..' part means taking the last part off that path: after a plain part it takes off that part, after the starting directory it takes off a directory, above the first directory it is kept. Hops 1-3 hold the two names and hop 4 the starting directory and the parts; none sees the walked path, and once the gold has built the module name the separators are '$' and no caller can tell a part from a directory. A one-line repair above the gold must re-implement the walk (for example PathUtil.makeAbsolute at hop 2 or PathUtil.collapseDots at hop 4, which also drop a '..' that climbs above the first directory, while the original java.net.URI resolution keeps it) or fit the trigger's names. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc promises 'relative addressing with ./ and ../ based on currentFilename'; hop 2 dispatches '../' names to the directory path; PathUtil.collapseDots ('a/b/../c' results in 'a/c'), used by PathUtil.makeAbsolute and PathUtil.makeRelative (DepsGenerator), takes a '..' off the preceding directory. The gold's javadoc promises the module name of the file that the parts lead to from the directory: [.., baz] leads from 'foo' to 'baz', whose module name is module$baz. The ownership tests pass on the variant and pin the neighbouring conventions of the same path: top-level names do not depend on the requiring file (testWithoutExports: 'mod/name' from 'test/sub' is module$mod$name), dashes become underscores and the extension is removed (testDash, testGuessModuleName, CompilerTest.testCommonJSProvidesAndRequire).
